hero_kpi_rationale: DocuSign generates 98% of its revenue through subscriptions, which ensures visibility and revenue predictability essential for a technology company.

kpis.name: Subscription Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by subscriptions to the company's products and services.
kpis.description: Subscription revenues constitute the majority of DocuSign's revenues, reflecting the cloud-based and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) business model.
kpis.signal: 98% of revenues come from subscriptions, a guarantee of stability.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin indicates the profitability of core operations before taking into account other expenses.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit expressed as a percentage of total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin measures the profitability of the company's core business activities.

kpis.name: R&D Investments
kpis.explanation: Total spending on research and development for innovation and new product development.
kpis.description: Indicates the company's investment in innovation and the development of new products or services.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Capital expenditures for the acquisition or upgrade of physical assets.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures represent the funds used by the company to acquire or improve its long-term assets.
kpis.signal: Investment in cloud and technology infrastructure.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees working for the company.
kpis.description: The number of employees can reflect the company's growth strategy, outsourcing approach, or cost reduction efforts.

kpis.name: Customer Growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in the total number of customers over a given period.
kpis.description: Customer growth is a key indicator of market penetration and product adoption.
kpis.signal: Growth in enterprise and commercial customer counts.

kpis.name: International Revenue Share
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total revenue generated outside the company's home country.
kpis.description: International revenue share demonstrates the extent of the company's global presence and its growth potential in foreign markets.

kpis.name: Customer Count
kpis.explanation: Total number of active customers using DocuSign solutions.
kpis.description: The total number of customers, including enterprises, SMBs, and micro-businesses, demonstrates the broad adoption of DocuSign solutions.

kpis.name: Large Customers (>$300k ACV)
kpis.explanation: Number of customers generating more than $300,000 in annual contract value.
kpis.description: This KPI highlights DocuSign's ability to attract and retain high-value customers, often large enterprises.
kpis.signal: Increase in large accounts and high-value customers.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks, including hacker attacks, which could compromise the confidentiality and integrity of its customers' data.

risks.title: Litigation
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to potential litigation related to intellectual property, which could result in significant costs and losses.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive market, which could lead to market share losses and pricing pressures.

risks.title: Regulation
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict regulations, including data protection requirements, which could result in additional costs and complexity.

risks.title: Technology Dependency
risks.score_rationale: The company is heavily dependent on the availability and stability of its technology infrastructure and cloud platforms.
